extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, IP professionals, industry, academia, and other IP stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of patent-related statistical indicators and definitions used to describe and evaluate patenting activity worldwide (applications, grants, families, stocks, technology fields, and related ratios). Intended to inform policy, research and IP practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications worldwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patent applications filed worldwide (annual total) and year-on-year growth rate (e.g., 'Patent applications worldwide grew by 3.6% in 2021').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a headline measure of global patenting activity; reported with time series (2007–2021) and comparisons to pre-COVID levels. Note: patent applications data refer to invention patents and do not include utility model applications (UM data reported separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident and non-resident filings (resident vs non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of applications into resident filings (filed at applicant's home office) and non-resident filings (filed abroad). Example: 'The 3.4 million applications comprised 2.4 million resident filings (70.1%) and 1 million non-resident filings (29.9%).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for understanding domestic vs international filing behavior and trends (e.g., decline in non-resident share due to growth in China). Definitions provided in glossary (non-resident = applicant not domiciled in office jurisdiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by office and office rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and ranking of patent applications received by national and regional IP offices (e.g., CNIPA, USPTO, JPO, KIPO, EPO), and share of world total per office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify top offices and their contribution to global filings; includes resident vs non-resident composition per office and changes in rankings over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident share per office
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of an office's applications that are non-resident (foreign) applications (e.g., 'non-resident applicants accounted for 90.8% at Australia').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how internationally-oriented filings to an office are; varies widely by office and affects interpretation of office volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application count
rubrics_metrics.description: A counting concept for regional offices where each regional application is multiplied by the corresponding number of member states (and special counting rules for ARIPO/EPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to report data by origin and to avoid undercounting applications filed at regional offices when attributing to country origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent families (unique inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent family: a set of interrelated patent applications filed at one or more offices to protect the same invention, interlinked by priority claims, PCT national phase entry, continuation, etc.; used to capture the number of unique inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent family indicators aim to minimize double counting of the same invention across jurisdictions; drawback: time lag (can be up to three years). WIPO's definition excludes families associated only with utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family size / geographical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of offices where a patent family is filed, reflecting the geographical coverage of protection (e.g., 'around 85% of patent families created 2017–2019 were filed at a single office').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to infer the internationalization of inventions and applicants' market/protection strategy; distributions vary by origin (e.g., many Chinese families filed at a single office).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent families
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families that have at least one filing office different from the applicant’s country of origin; may sometimes include only one filing office when applicant files directly abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to measure international protection efforts by origin; note that a foreign-oriented family can be single-office if the applicant filed directly at a foreign office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications by technology field (IPC-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of published patent applications across technology fields defined via IPC symbols (e.g., computer technology, electrical machinery, measurement, digital communications, medical technology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPC-based definitions and mappings to technology fields are used (Annex A); caveat that correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always clear-cut, so definitions may not capture all related patents perfectly. Reported shares and growth rates by field (e.g., computer technology = 10.2% of published applications in 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications and abroad filings by origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of equivalent patent applications originating from a country (resident plus abroad filings) and the number of applications filed abroad by applicants from that origin (abroad filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare domestic vs international filing intensity of origins (e.g., China had low share filed abroad, US and Germany had high shares). Helps rank origins by global activity (e.g., top origins by equivalent applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP (patent-to-GDP ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications normalized by GDP (applications per USD 100 billion GDP) to account for economic size (e.g., Republic of Korea: 8,159 per USD 100 billion GDP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows cross-country comparisons adjusting for economic size; rankings and trends over time reported (e.g., China improved patent-to-GDP ratio markedly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per million population (patent-to-population ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications normalized by population to assess filings relative to country size (e.g., Republic of Korea: 3,599 per million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complementary to patent-to-GDP; rankings are similar with some differences in order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grants (patents granted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patents granted by offices in a year and growth rates (e.g., an estimated 1.76 million patents were granted worldwide in 2021, up 10% on 2020).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant counts depend on examination capacity and procedural differences across offices; application data for a given year should not be compared directly with grant data from the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force (stock of active patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated number of patents in force across jurisdictions at a point in time (e.g., 16.5 million patents in force across 133 jurisdictions in 2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects cumulative active protection; influenced by maintenance/renewal payments and lapse decisions. Reported breakdowns by jurisdiction, changes, average age, and proportion remaining in force after specified years (e.g., share remaining for at least 8 years and for full 20-year term).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance / renewal (renewal fees and survival rates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Act by applicant to keep an IP grant/registration valid by paying required renewal/maintenance fees; metric often reported as proportion of grants remaining in force after X years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical for interpretation of patents in force; example: about 40.3% of patents granted remained in force for at least 8 years after filing, and about 18.1% lasted the full 20-year term (based on 92 reporting offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of patent examination outcomes (granted, rejected, withdrawn/abandoned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of processed applications resulting in grant, rejection, or withdrawal/abandonment for offices (e.g., China rejected 34.4% of processed applications; US rejected 45.2%; Canada had 35.8% withdrawn/abandoned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate examination rigor and applicant behavior; absolute numbers and shares reported. Cross-office comparisons require care due to procedural differences and coverage of reporting offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pending applications (stock and backlog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number (or stock) of patent applications pending examination at an office in a given year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates office workload and delay; pending stocks are reported (China recorded highest stock in 2021). Relevant because offices must assess claims against patentability standards (novelty, inventive step/non-obviousness, industrial applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability standards (novelty, non-obviousness/inventive step, industrial applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core substantive standards used by offices when examining claims: novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability (utility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the legal/technical criteria applied during substantive examination to determine whether claims are patentable; mentioned as the standards offices assess claims against when processing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grant rate (grants per applications processed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of processed applications that result in a grant for a given office or set of offices (e.g., 'Germany, Türkiye and the US granted patents for under half of all applications processed in 2021').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an indicator of examination outcomes and selectivity; influenced by office procedures and applicant selection; compare cautiously across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology/industry classification mappings (IPC, Nice, Locarno)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mappings that link IPC symbols to technology fields (Annex A) and mappings of industry sectors to Nice classes (Annex B) and Locarno classes (Annex C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classification mappings are used to aggregate and report patent, trademark and design statistics by technology and industry sector; caution that mappings are imperfect and may not capture all related items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-series and growth indicators (trend analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of multi-year time series and growth rates to interpret patent activity trends (e.g., long-term upward trend, decade comparisons, largest year-on-year drops or recoveries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-series context is emphasized for interpretation (e.g., 2019 patent family drop of 7.5%); short-term year-to-year changes may be driven by specific large offices and should be interpreted with contextual explanation.
